question: In △ABC, BD ⟂ AC at D and ∠DBC = 54°. E is a point on BC such that ∠CAE = 72°. What is the measure of ∠AEB?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In right-angled △BDC, ∠C = 180° − (90° + 54°) = 36°.

In △AEC, the exterior angle at vertex E is ∠AEB.

According to the exterior angle theorem, an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

⇒ ∠AEB = ∠C + ∠CAE

⇒ ∠AEB = 36° + 72° = 108°.

**∴ The correct answer is 108°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

• BD ⊥ AC at D

• ∠DBC = 54°

• E is a point on BC such that ∠CAE = 72°

**Formula Used:**

• Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°

• Angles on a straight line (linear pair) add up to 180°

**Calculations:**

⇒ In right-angled △BDC, ∠BDC = 90° because BD is perpendicular to AC.

⇒ ∠C = 180° − (90° + 54°) = 36°.

⇒ Now, consider △AEC. The sum of all its internal angles must be 180°.

⇒ ∠CAE + ∠C + ∠AEC = 180°

⇒ 72° + 36° + ∠AEC = 180°

⇒ 108° + ∠AEC = 180°

⇒ ∠AEC = 180° − 108° = 72°

⇒ Since points B, E, and C lie on a straight line, ∠AEB and ∠AEC form a linear pair.

⇒ ∠AEB + ∠AEC = 180°

⇒ ∠AEB + 72° = 180°

⇒ ∠AEB = 180° − 72° = 108°

**∴ The correct answer is 108°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle is always equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles. Here, ∠AEB is an exterior angle to △AEC, allowing direct calculation: ∠AEB = ∠CAE + ∠C.

Isosceles Triangle Property

In any triangle, if two angles are equal, the sides opposite those angles are also equal in length. In △AEC, ∠CAE = ∠AEC = 72°, making it an isosceles triangle with AC = CE.

Linear Pair of Angles

When two adjacent angles are formed by intersecting lines and their non-common sides form a straight line, they are known as a linear pair. Their sum is always 180°.
